claims.statement: Parent Atlas separates infrastructure-free contracts, infrastructure-backed runtime adapters, protocol clients, agent wrappers, and service endpoints with one-way dependencies: runtime implements contracts, clients depend on contracts but not runtime, and agent wrappers reach runtime through clients rather than direct calls.

Protocol adapters are transport boundaries rather than retrieval engines: HTTP, gRPC, MCP, and A2A delegate to the retrieval facade, while ranking, deduplication, and graph traversal remain outside protocol clients and handlers.

PostgreSQL remains the canonical packet, source, workspace identity, and provenance authority; proposed registry metadata must retain foreign-key and revision linkage to PostgreSQL rather than creating a second packet identity store.
Qdrant, Neo4j, caches, queues, export formats, and embedding lanes are lookup, graph-proof, cache, work, transport, or projection surfaces and must not be treated as canonical packet identity stores.

Retrieval must resolve candidates to canonical identity before reciprocal-rank fusion; otherwise duplicate representations can receive multiple ranking contributions, while documented failures permit BM25-only or core-candidate fallback.

The packet registry centralizes the title generator version and canonical title_id format, and title backfills are prohibited from modifying packet_key, source_ref, feature_id, tree_node_id, or qdrant_point_id; only title fields and updated_at are declared writable.

The revision-qualified registry design records distinct logical executor lanes and requires projection health to be checked by independent readback and checksums against PostgreSQL packet and source revisions; mirrors must not add retrieval votes merely because they contain the same packet.

The data-spine workflow is dry-run by default and requires an explicit --write gate for external database or vector writes; the registry change separately excludes automatic migrations, backfills, Qdrant writes, cache warming, promotion, and direct Mastra or LangGraph durable writes.

The semantic-AST RPC is designed as read-only and carries workspace or packet revisions, source references, AST spans, parser or grammar revisions, and receipts; a separate gated producer-admission path is required for writes.

Drizzle migration policy distinguishes journaled SQL, documented sidecars, and undocumented pending SQL: documented sidecars are intentional and informational, while unjournaled and undocumented numbered SQL is classified as a stale migration rather than silently executed.

The registry design leaves several boundaries unresolved: the final registry relation, the authorized first AST producer, and whether the FastAPI GPU lane speaks gRPC directly or remains behind a Go adapter require further implementation or live-schema decisions.

The `atlas_packets` Drizzle schema treats PostgreSQL as the packet identity spine and stores packet, source, workspace, representation, embedding-lineage, and Qdrant reference fields as distinct lineage anchors; storing a Qdrant, Neo4j, or Redis reference in the row does not transfer authority to that external system.

Parent Atlas keeps acquisition identities separate: research runs, fetches, fetch attempts, digest-deduplicated source revisions, and extractor-specific extractions are different lifecycle records, so a fetch or extraction identity must not replace source-revision authority.

The workspace-event schema mirror records checksummed event and head revisions but explicitly leaves the manual sidecar as migration authority and declares `applied: false` and `writesPerformed: false`, so the mirror cannot prove live database application.

The current tRPC `getPacketRegistry` procedure intentionally returns an unavailable, non-authoritative result because the live schema lacks a canonical packet-revision owner and closed packet/source/AST joins; its focused test requires `UNAVAILABLE`, `canonicalAuthority: false`, and `writesPerformed: false`.

The current lane census is conservative observability rather than parity proof: PostgreSQL BM25 is `READY` and `READ_ONLY`, pgvector is `DEGRADED`, Qdrant is `DEGRADED` and `PROJECTION_ONLY`, and cuVS or FastAPI are `UNPROVEN` and `PROJECTION_ONLY`; lane descriptors carry status, model, representation, collection, index, checksum, and write-policy fields.

The implemented evidence service preserves the caller's workspace revision, selects retrieval lanes, and validates the output, while the parallel orchestrator uses `Promise.allSettled`, aggregates lane outcomes, deduplicates by result identity, and blends scores before returning top-K results.

SvelteKit server hooks enforce request-level size, rate, authentication, authorization, timeout, and cache controls at the entrypoint; these controls protect access and transport behavior but do not grant handlers ownership of PostgreSQL, Qdrant, Neo4j, or Valkey state.

The packet-registry semantic-AST schema requires a revision-qualified identity tuple and validates AST byte-span ordering, while the registry entry schema makes lane status and write policy explicit; these contracts qualify transported data without making RPC the owner.

The current title-writer compatibility regression pin classifies all known title writers, requires every result to be non-persistence-eligible, and surfaces registry-version drift, making compatibility classification a safety gate rather than evidence that a backfill is authorized.

The index-stream boundary tests require Qdrant content vectors to stay out of the PostgreSQL canonical semantic lane and require the PostgreSQL mirror to receive metadata without the Qdrant content vector.
The package-boundary verifier checks declared package exports, owner paths, forbidden mirrors, required package imports, and runtime imports before reporting package-boundary readiness.
